- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for days 1–5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), model tends to lag; forecast should be 0.5–1.0% above recent 7-day average to capture momentum.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply 1–2% upward correction in first 2–3 days of sentiment change.
